summary: Improve cadastral data, parcel identification and land-service workflows with applied GIS training. Explore the five-day course and request details.
lede: Land information systems training helps land administrators, surveyors, GIS officers, planners and valuers organize parcel records for land-service decisions. It covers checking cadastral data quality, matching parcel identifiers, linking tenure and valuation records, and mapping municipal workflows in QGIS. Learners also review metadata and fit-for-purpose survey coverage and create a phased improvement plan using sample cadastral data; advanced database engineering and automated model deployment are outside the course’s implementation scope.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who create, maintain, analyze or use land information systems in land administration, municipal services and infrastructure planning.
prerequisites: Prior exposure to land administration, surveying, municipal planning, property valuation or GIS is recommended. You should be comfortable reading basic maps or land records; programming is not required. Bring a laptop if you will take part in QGIS exercises. Confirm software access and any exercise-data arrangements with the course coordinator before delivery.
